skill.name: azure-data-tables-java
skill.description: Build Java applications with the Azure Tables SDK for Azure Table Storage and Cosmos DB Table API.
skill.summary: Create, query, update, and manage Azure Tables data from Java applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, Java sample code, placeholder Azure endpoints, and typed-entity setters. No prompt injection, malicious intent, command execution path, or data exfiltration behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Credential placeholders appear in setup examples.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders clearly marked and remind users to store real secrets in secure configuration or managed identity flows.

remediation.issue: Examples use a beta SDK dependency version.
remediation.suggestion: Review the SDK version before publication and prefer a stable release when it supports the documented features.

content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable patterns for Azure Table Storage and Cosmos DB Table API. This skill provides focused examples for clients, entities, queries, batches, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure Tables Java SDK.
Demonstrates client creation with connection strings, shared keys, SAS tokens, and DefaultAzureCredential.
Provides examples for table creation, table lookup, entity CRUD, and upsert operations.
Explains entity listing, OData filters, projection, and top result limits.
Covers same-partition batch transactions and basic TableServiceException handling.
limitations: Does not validate live Azure credentials or provision cloud resources.
Uses example placeholders that must be replaced with environment-specific values.
Does not cover every SDK option, retry policy, or production monitoring pattern.
Examples require testing against the selected Azure Table Storage or Cosmos DB account.

use_cases.title: Implement Table CRUD
use_cases.description: Add create, read, update, upsert, delete, and list operations to a Java service.

use_cases.title: Plan Query Patterns
use_cases.description: Design PartitionKey and RowKey usage with filters, projections, and result limits.

use_cases.title: Migrate Table API Code
use_cases.description: Adapt code paths for Azure Table Storage or Cosmos DB Table API using the same SDK concepts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure Tables Java client for [Azure Storage or Cosmos DB] using [credential type].

prompt_templates.title: Add Entity CRUD
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate Java examples for creating, reading, updating, upserting, deleting, and listing entities in table [table name].

prompt_templates.title: Design an OData Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write an Azure Tables Java query for entities where [conditions], selecting only [properties], and explain the PartitionKey impact.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Table Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Azure Tables Java workflow for batch limits, partition design, update mode choice, and error handling gaps: [paste workflow summary].

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to connect to Azure Table Storage from Java.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the right client builder, credential option, endpoint value, and required Maven dependency.

output_examples.input: A team needs to update inventory records without replacing every property.
output_examples.output: The response recommends merge updates, shows the required entity keys, and explains when replace mode is appropriate.

output_examples.input: An architect wants faster product lookups by category.
output_examples.output: The response focuses on PartitionKey design, filtered queries, selected properties, and result limits.

best_practices: Use PartitionKey values that distribute load and match common query paths.
Use projection to return only properties needed by the caller.
Test credential, endpoint, retry, and error handling behavior in the target Azure environment.
anti_patterns: Do not store real connection strings, account keys, or SAS tokens in prompts or source files.
Do not query broad table ranges when a PartitionKey filter is available.
Do not use replace updates when merge updates better protect existing properties.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Cosmos DB Table API?
faq.answer: Yes. The source states that the Azure Tables SDK examples apply to Azure Table Storage and Cosmos DB Table API.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples. You must create and configure resources separately.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers connection strings, shared keys, SAS tokens, and DefaultAzureCredential for supported storage scenarios.

faq.question: Can it help with entity modeling?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TableEntity examples and a typed entity pattern with PartitionKey and RowKey fields.

faq.question: Does it include batch transaction guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows transaction actions and notes that all entities in a batch need the same partition key.

faq.question: Is production validation still required?
faq.answer: Yes. You should validate credentials, permissions, retry behavior, and performance in your Azure environment.
